new_findings.description: RULE-001 §5 case 5 introduces a 'Residual known bypass' category — explicitly naming the case where technically-compliant inputs satisfy the rule's syntactic check but not its semantic intent (URL exists but does not necessarily point to a decision artifact). This is a valuable and non-obvious category for any rule that enforces a syntactic pattern (URL, regex, format) rather than semantic validity. RULE-TEMPLATE.md §5 does not guide future authors toward enumerating this category. A next-RFC author following only RULE-TEMPLATE.md will document explicit new bypass mechanisms and the four structural no-op cases, but will miss the residual-bypass framing unless they read RULE-001 as a worked example. The gap is in the template, not in RULE-001 (which is correct).
new_findings.recommendation: File as TF-020L-002. Closure path: amend RULE-TEMPLATE.md §5 implicit exclusion set guidance to add a note: 'If the rule enforces a syntactic pattern (URL, regex, format constraint) rather than semantic validity of the matched value, add a case N "Residual known bypass" naming the gap between syntactic compliance and semantic intent — and the closure path (e.g. a future SCP-R-NNN with stricter domain checks, or explicit acknowledgment that honest-actor posture accepts the residual). See RULE-001 §5 case 5 as a worked example.' This prevents future RFCs from silently omitting the residual-bypass category.

new_findings.description: README.md §3 Merge states 'An entry in docs/DECISIONS.md if the rule introduces a new domain or escalates an existing rule's threshold.' The phrase 'new domain' is undefined. RULE-001 §9 takes the position that SCP-R-004 is same-domain as SCP-R-002 (waivers domain). This is plausible and well-argued. However, future proposal authors will face the same ambiguity: does 'new domain' mean (a) a new top-level policy area with a distinct input schema, (b) any rule that doesn't share a schema with an existing rule, or (c) something else? Without a definition, the D-NNN filing decision is operator-judgment-dependent for every subsequent RFC. The gap does not block RULE-001 (which commits explicitly to a position), but it will recur on RULE-002+.
new_findings.recommendation: File as TF-020L-003. Closure path: amend README.md §3 Merge to define 'new domain': 'A rule introduces a new domain if it evaluates a distinctly different input type (a new top-level input schema not addressed by any existing SCP-R-NNN rule) or a policy area that has no existing SCP-R-NNN counterpart. Adding a new constraint on the same input schema as an existing rule (e.g. an additional field-level check on the waivers payload already governed by SCP-R-002) is same-domain and does not require a merge-time D-NNN.' This definition makes RULE-001 §9's position canonical and eliminates future judgment-call ambiguity.

new_findings.description: The §Labels section sits between §Authorship guidance and §Auto-defer mechanics. The Authorship guidance section is not about labels; the jump from authorship advice to label provisioning is a minor narrative break. The Auto-defer mechanics section directly depends on the 'defer' label existing, so placing Labels immediately before Auto-defer mechanics is the most coherent position. The current placement (with Authorship guidance in between) is a readability issue only — no process gap arises because the labels are documented and the cross-references from §Process step 2 and §3 are present.
new_findings.recommendation: Optional: move §Authorship guidance after §Labels if the document is ever restructured. No action required at this merge.

summary.verdict_rationale: All 10 R1 completeness findings are correctly closed (8 inline, 1 correctly deferred to merge, 1 acknowledged as Phase-2 hint). Zero new CRIT/MAJ on this complete cycle. Two new MIN findings are filed as TF-020L-002 and TF-020L-003 — both are template/README gaps that do not affect RULE-001's correctness or the proposal's merge-readiness; they affect future RFCs only. The most consequential new finding is COMP-R2-MIN-001: RULE-TEMPLATE.md §5 lacks the 'Residual known bypass' example category that RULE-001 §5 case 5 introduces — without this template update, subsequent RFC authors will not know to enumerate syntactic-vs-semantic bypass gaps. TF-020L-002 captures the closure path.
